newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Telkom mulls launching cable television.
newsitem.headline: Telkom mulls launching cable television.

text.p: Indonesia's telecommunications giant PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) said on Wednesday it was studying the possibility of launching a cable television network.

"We are currently studying the possibility of launching cable television. Telkom's role would be to provide the high-speed telephone network for the cable tv services," Investor Relations Manager Thomas Widjanarto told Reuters.
Widjanarto declined to say when the state-controlled firm was likely to launch cable television services, adding that a thorough study was needed.
"The cost of building the network is not small. Telkom also needs partners to provide the broadcasting and the content," Widjanarto said.
He said Telkom, which is also listed in New York and London, had received proposals from privately-owned firms to launch the cable services.
Widjanarto declined to comment on whether Telkom planned to set up a new joint venture firm to launch the cable network or carry out the project through its multimedia unit PT Telemedia Indonesia.

Telemedia, set up in October 1996, is 35-percent owned by Telkom and 25 percent owned by PT Asriland. PT Telekomindo Prima Bhakti and PT Rajawali Citra Televisi Indonesia each owns 20 percent. The three Telkom partners are private-owned firms.
